ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hūd's zeal for monotheism makes him interrupt the accusation, disavow the idolaters, and challenge them to harm him without delay.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: his sense of honour for monotheism was roused

STUDYQURAN:11:55/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r1.claim: Other prophets make similar statements about the beliefs of the people to whom they were sent.
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r1.anchor: For similar statements made by prophets concerning the beliefs of the people to whom they had been sent, see also 6:19; 6:78.

STUDYQURAN:11:55/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r2.speaker: N
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r2.claim: N notes that Hūd addresses his challenge to both his people and their gods.
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r2.anchor: Hūd’s challenge, which is addressed to his people and their gods (N), to scheme and grant him no respite means

STUDYQURAN:11:55/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r3.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r3.claim: Kl explains the challenge as meaning that neither the people nor their gods can do anything against Hūd.
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r3.anchor: means, “Neither you nor your gods will be able to do anything!” (Kl). Hūd then provides them

TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r1.claim: After his people accused him of being harmed for condemning their idols, Hud disavows their worship and challenges them and their gods to plot against him without delay.
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r1.anchor: يقول: فاحتالوا أنتم جميعا وآلهتكم في ضري ومكروهي،

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r6.claim: The command to plot and prohibition on delaying are deliberately impossible challenges.

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.claim: Hūd challenges them so they can see that their gods neither harm him nor avenge themselves; their inaction proves the gods are powerless and did not afflict him.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.anchor: ولو كانت آلهة ذات علم وقدرة لقهرته وانتقمت منه لنفسها كما ادعوا أن بعض آلهتهم اعتراه بسوء

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r8.claim: They also see that despite their strength they cannot kill or punish Hūd; if he were not God's truthful prophet and protected by Him, they could have harmed him.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r8.anchor: ثم يشاهدوا من أنفسهم أنهم لا يقدرون عليه بقتل أو تنكيل مع كونهم ذوي شدة وقوة

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.claim: The response supplies a rational proof against the partners’ divinity: Hūd’s disavowal exposes their false godhood and the claim that one harmed him.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.anchor: مشتمل على حجة عقلية على بطلان ألوهية الشركاء

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.claim: The challenge, followed by Hūd’s remaining unharmed among them, is also a miraculous sign confirming his message.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.anchor: وعلى آية معجزة لصحة رسالة هود عليه السلام

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r4.claim: “All together” includes both the people and all their idols in the challenge, making the proof of Hūd’s truth and their falsehood more complete.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r4.anchor: مراده تعجيزهم وتعجيز آلهتهم جميعا فيكون أتم دلالة

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r5.claim: The imperative could mean Hūd does not fear them even if they can harm him, as in the magicians’ words to Pharaoh; he follows it with reliance on God to rule out that reading.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r5.anchor: لأن يكون المراد به إظهار أنه لا يخافهم وإن فعلوا به ما فعلوا

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.claim: ʿĀd were prehistoric Arab inhabitants of the peninsula; their history survives only in unreliable tales, and the extant Torah does not mention them.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.anchor: عاد قوم هود هؤلاء قوم من العرب من بشر ما قبل التاريخ كانوا يسكنون الجزيرة انقطعت أخبارهم وانمحت آثارهم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.claim: The Quran places ʿĀd after Noah in al-Aḥqāf; the name may be “first ʿĀd,” suggesting a second ʿĀd as well.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.anchor: كانوا قوما يسكنون الأحقاف من شبه جزيرة العرب بعد قوم نوح

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.claim: The people were tall, strong, and physically imposing, with advanced urban life, thriving towns, fertile land, gardens, date palms, and crops.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.anchor: كانت لهم أجساد طويلة وكانوا ذوي بسطة في الخلق أولي قوة وبطش شديد وكان لهم تقدم ورقي في المدينة والحضارة

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.claim: After enjoying God’s bounty, they developed idolatry, built monuments on every rise and grand structures as if to live forever, and obeyed arrogant tyrants.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.anchor: لم يزل القوم يتنعمون بنعمة الله حتى غيروا ما بأنفسهم فتعرقت فيهم الوثنية وبنوا بكل ريع آية يعبثون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.claim: God sent their kinsman Hūd to call them to truth, worship of God, rejection of idols, justice, and mercy; he admonished them and made the way clear.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.anchor: فبعث الله إليهم أخاهم هودا يدعوهم إلى الحق ويرشدهم إلى أن يعبدوا الله ويرفضوا الأوثان

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.claim: Only a small group believed; most persisted in defiance, called Hūd foolish and mad, and demanded the threatened punishment, to which he replied that its timing belongs to God.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.anchor: وأصر جمهورهم على البغي والعناد، ورموه بالسفه والجنون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.claim: God sent a barren, furious wind through adverse days, lasting seven nights and eight days; it left the people fallen like hollow palm trunks and destroyed them all but their dwellings.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.anchor: وأرسل إليهم الريح العقيم ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.claim: They first mistook the cloud approaching their valleys for rain, but it was the very calamity they had demanded; God annihilated them and saved Hūd and the believers by His mercy.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.anchor: وكانوا بادئ ما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم استبشروا وقالوا عارض ممطرنا وقد أخطأوا بل كان هو الذي استعجلوا به

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.claim: Hūd was from ʿĀd and the second prophet whose struggle against idolatry and suffering for God the Quran narrates; God praises him among the noble messengers.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.anchor: وأما هود عليه السلام فهو من قوم عاد وثاني الأنبياء الذين انتهضوا للدفاع عن الحق ودحض الوثنية ممن ذكر الله قصته وما قاساه

TABRISI:11:50-60/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60/r4.claim: “Inẓār” means granting someone respite to consider his affairs; “ta'khīr” simply means putting something later rather than earlier.
TABRISI:11:50-60/r4.anchor: والفرق بين الإنظار والتأخير أن الإنظار إمهال

TABRISI:11:50-60/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60/r9.claim: For “ghayruhu,” the nominative reading follows syntactic position, while the genitive follows the word's surface form.
TABRISI:11:50-60/r9.anchor: من ضم الراء حمل الصفة على الموضع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r1.claim: Hud challenges them and their idols to plot against him, show hostility, anger, or strike him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r1.anchor: أي احتالوا أنتم وأوثانكم في عداوتي وغيظي وضربي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r2.claim: Do not delay or give me respite.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r2.anchor: لا تمهلون، في قول ابن عباس (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r4.claim: This is among the greatest prophetic signs: Hud faces his numerous, united enemies because he trusts God's aid and knows they cannot reach him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬4) وغيره من أهل المعاني: هذا من أعظم آيات الأنبياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r5.claim: Noah likewise challenged his people to assemble their plans and partners and not give him respite.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447/r5.anchor: وكذلك قال نوح لقومه: {فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم} إلى قوله: {ولا تنظرون}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r8.claim: Hud tells them and their idols to conspire together against him.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r9.claim: He challenges them not to delay or give him respite.

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r6.claim: Hud challenges all the people and all their idols to scheme against him at once, without delay, asking what clearer proof of his confidence could be given.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r6.anchor: Yani bundan daha açık ne beyyine arıyorsunuz, yalnız bana fenalık getirdiğini iddia ettiğiniz bazısı değil bütün şerikleriniz ve siz hepiniz toplanarak bana fenalık yapmak için dilediğiniz planı kurun

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r5.claim: Hud challenged them all to act against him, thereby refuting their claim that their gods could harm him; he trusted and submitted to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r5.anchor: Tanrılarının aklını almış olması iddiasına karşılık da hepsine meydan okuyarak bu iddiayı çürüttü

SULAMI:v1p320/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p320/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p320/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says Hūd's state of connection and nearness made him fully present; his challenge to his opponents came from direct witnessing, seeing no one besides God.
SULAMI:v1p320/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : غلب على هود عليه السلام في ذلك الوقت الحال والوصلة والقربة

SULAMI:v1p320/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p320/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p320/r3.claim: Al-Wasiti says Hūd spoke from direct witnessing, seeing no one besides God.
SULAMI:v1p320/r3.anchor: وقال في هود : ﴿ فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون ﴾ [ الآية : 55 ] . نطق عن مشاهدة

SULAMI:v1p320/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p320/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p320/r4.claim: One gloss says Hūd challenges his opponents while held in God's grasp, might, and awe; plotting only reaches one captive to opposition.
SULAMI:v1p320/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : أي كيدوني بالحق من هو في قبضة الحق

ITQAN:v2p343/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r6.claim: Wa-lā tunẓirūn means do not delay or give me respite.

SAMIN-DURR:11:55/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:55/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:55/r1.claim: جميعا is a circumstantial accusative from the subject of فكيدون.

SAMIN-DURR:11:55/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:55/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:55/r2.claim: All other readers retain the yāʾ of فكيدوني at pause and in connection, and all omit it in 77:39.
SAMIN-DURR:11:55/r2.anchor: وأثبت سائر القراء ياء " فكيدوني " في الحالين، وحذفوها في المرسلات.

ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r14.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r14.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r14.claim: A messenger's great sign is to stand alone against a united people and challenge them to scheme without respite, though they cannot harm him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r14.anchor: وهذه من أعظم آيات الرسل أن يكون الرسول وحده

ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r15.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r15.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r15.claim: Hud's challenge is compared with Noah's challenge to his people to gather their plans and partners and then act without delay.

ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r1.speaker: محمد
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r1.claim: Muhammad is quoted as saying, If you have a plan, then scheme against me.
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r1.anchor: وقال محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r2.claim: The messengers' ability to issue this challenge is among the greatest and clearest signs of their messengership.
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r2.anchor: فهذه هن أعظم آيات الرسل وأدلها على رسالاتهم

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n79/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n79/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n79/r1.claim: Hud's challenge closely resembles the challenge in the final sentence of 7:195.
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n79/r1.anchor: a very similar challenge in the last sentence of 7:195

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.claim: The fully pronounced first-person yā form recurs in its surah more than the shortened form recurs in its own context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.anchor: وقد تتردد الكلمة ذات الياء المظهرة في السورة أكثر من تردد الكلمة ذات الياء المجتزأة في موطنها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.claim: Hud’s passage is an intense confrontation, so Hud openly presents himself as challenger; Araf lacks that same setting.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.anchor: فإن المقام في هود مقام تحدٍّ كبير ومواجهة، فأظهر نفسه زيادة في التحدي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.claim: After they allege that some deity harmed him, Hud disavows their gods and challenges them all; “all” answers their “some.”
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.anchor: فزاد كلمة: (جميعاً) زيادة في التحدي رداً على قولهم: {إِن نَّقُولُ إِلاَّ اعتراك بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنَا بسواء}

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.claim: Hud’s challenge and confrontation are longer than Araf’s; the longer yā form suits Hud, while the shortened form suits Araf’s briefer context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.anchor: إن التحدي والمواجهة في هود أطول وأكثر مما في الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.claim: Hud repeatedly uses the first-person yā in this passage, whereas Araf shows it only once, in “Indeed, my protector is Allah”; this repetition suits Hud.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.anchor: ومن ناحية أخرى نرى أنه قد تردد ذكر ياء الضمير في هود في هذا الموطن مرات عديدة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.claim: Araf places then before the challenge and fa before denying respite; Hud reverses them. Fa signals immediacy, then delay.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.anchor: والفاء تفيد التعقيب أما (ثم) فتفيد التراخي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.claim: The immediate denial of respite fits Araf’s early emphasis on swift worldly punishment, while Hud’s context stresses respite and delayed punishment.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.anchor: وعدم الإنظار هو المناسب لسياق الأعراف، فقد ذكر في هذه السورة تعجيل العقوبات لمستحقيها في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.claim: Araf’s Noah story is concise and moves directly from denial to rescue and drowning; Hud’s longer exchange lets Noah’s people demand the promised punishment and await it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.anchor: أما في هود فالكلام طويل وهناك مهلة حتى استبطؤوا ما وعدهم به

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.claim: Araf’s account of ʿĀd presents their punishment swiftly, while Hud gives a fuller account after the divine command, including their worldly curse and fate on Judgment Day.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.anchor: فانظر كيف عجّل العقوبة لهم في الأعراف فجاء بالفاء الدالة على عدم الإمهال، بخلاف ما في سورة هود

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.claim: Araf says the earthquake seized Ṣāliḥ’s people with fa, showing swift punishment; Hud describes their rescue and says the wrongdoers were seized without that fa sequence.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.anchor: فذكر إنزال العقوبة بالفاء في الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.claim: Where Araf combines then and fa, then comes first; in Hud the order is reversed, as in the cited challenge and other examples.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.anchor: وهنالك أمر فني آخر، وهو أنه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.claim: As a general rule, when the yāʾ is written out the context is extended and detailed; where kasra stands in for it, the expression is concise, apart from verse endings and vocatives.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.anchor: أن الاجتزاء بالكسرة عن الياء يختلف عن ذكر الياء في كل ما ورد في القرآن الكريم عدا خواتم الآي والنداء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.claim: He adds that the yāʾ is audibly repeated more often in places where it is written than in places where kasra replaces it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.anchor: ومن ناحية أخرى إن الياء تتردد مُظهرةً في المواطن التي تذكر فيها الياء أكثر من المواطن التي يجتزأ بالكسرة عنها

NASHR:v2p292/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p292/r10.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p292/r10.claim: Yaqub retains the extra yāʾ in ثم لا تنظروني both in connection and at pause.
NASHR:v2p292/r10.anchor: ثم لا تنظروني أثبتها في الحالين يعقوب

QIRAAT-ER:11:55:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:55:8#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:11:55:8#1/r1.claim: Adding yāʾ after nūn al-wiqāya extends the first person pronoun phonetically without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:11:55:8#1/r1.anchor: Addition of yāʾ after nūn al-wiqāya — phonetic extension of the 1s pronoun; no semantic change

IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r1.speaker: عمير بن عدي
IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r1.claim: After returning from the Prophet, Umayr ibn Adi told Banu Khatma he had killed Marwan's daughter and challenged them to retaliate; this became the first public sign of Islam's strength among them.
IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r1.anchor: فلما جاءهم عمير بن عدي من عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: يا بني خطمة، أنا قتلت ابنة مروان

IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r2.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r2.claim: Islam had been concealed among Banu Khatma; Umayr was their first Muslim, followed by Abdullah ibn Aws and Khuzayma ibn Thabit, and others embraced Islam that day after seeing its strength.
IBNHISHAM:v2p638/r2.anchor: وكان أول من أسلم من بني خطمة عمير بن عدي، وهو الذي يدعى القارئ، وعبد الله بن أوس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.claim: Hud's repudiation and challenge, despite facing a united crowd eager to kill him, displays sincerity and confidence in God's promised support and protection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.anchor: وعدم تأخره من أعظم الآيات على صدقه وثقته بموعود ربه من النصر له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r12.claim: Hud's challenge resembles Noah's challenge to his people to carry out their decision without delay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r12.anchor: ومثله قول نوح لقومه: ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r11.claim: Hūd challenges them all to gather with every idol and cooperate in harming him, then forbids them to delay.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r11.anchor: الإجتماع والإحتشاد مع آلهتهم جميعا دون بعض منها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r1.claim: If their hint that their gods can harm him is true, they should all join the gods and attack without delay; the فاء derives the challenge from both their claim and his disavowal.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r1.anchor: فالفاء لتفريع الأمر على زعمهم من قدرة آلهتهم على ما قالوا وعلى البراءة كليهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r2.claim: The address can include both the people and their gods; some understand it as addressed to the people alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r2.anchor: والخطاب للقوم وآلهتهم ويفهم من كلام بعض أنه للقوم فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r3.claim: If even a united crowd of powerful people cannot harm him, lifeless idols are all the more powerless; the challenge thus proves their gods cannot harm him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r3.anchor: فإن الأقوياء الأشداء إذا لم يقدروا مع إجتماعهم واحتشادهم على الضر كان عدم قدرة الجمادات عليه معلوما من باب أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r4.claim: On one reported account, Hūd stood alone among tyrants thirsty for his blood, challenged and belittled them, yet they could do nothing; this was a manifest miracle and showed his trust in God's protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83/r4.anchor: إنه كان عليه السلام مفردا بين جمع عتاة جبابرة عطاش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.claim: The phrase refers to the idols besides God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.claim: Hūd challenges them and their idols to devise their plot and harm against him together.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.anchor: فكيدوني جميعا} فاحتالوا في مكركم (2) وضري أنتم وأوثانكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.claim: He tells them not to delay or grant him respite.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r7.claim: He contemptuously tells them to unite and try to kill him without delay; if they fail, they must concede their lifeless idols cannot harm him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r7.anchor: وأن يجتمعوا على الكيد في إهلاكه من غير إنظار

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r8.claim: His bold challenge before a fierce crowd is a miracle grounded in trust in God, while their failure to hurt him shows divine protection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r8.anchor: فإن مواجهة الواحد الجم الغفير من الجبابرة الفتاك

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r9.claim: The account leads into Hud’s explanation that trust in God makes threats powerless.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r9.anchor: ليس إلا لثقته بالله وتثبطهم عن إضراره ليس إلا بعصمته إياه ولذلك عقبه بقوله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r6.claim: Hūd challenges them to plot against him all together, individually if they choose, or collectively with their idols.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r6.anchor: { فكيدوني } حال كونكم { جميعا } أي فرادى إن شئتم أو مجتمعين أنتم وآلهتكم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r7.claim: Because an immediate attack is more alarming and difficult, the particle thumma intensifies the challenge to give him no respite.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r7.anchor: ولما كانت المعاجلة في الحرب أهول , وكان شأنها أصعب وأخطر , بين عظمها بأداة التراخي فقال : { ثم لا تنظرون * }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r8.claim: Kayd is a covert scheme intended to provoke or inflict vexation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r8.anchor: والكيد : طلب الغيظ بالسر في مكر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r9.claim: This fearless challenge is a clear sign of Hūd's prophethood.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية من أعلام النبوة الواضحة لهود عليه السلام

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r1.speaker: محمد بن مهاجر
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Muhajir recounts Umar telling his relatives to scheme against him without delay and insisting that kinship gave them no special claim; they dispersed afterward.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن مهاجر قال : كان عمر جالسا وهو يشق عليه الجلوس فكان متكئا وعنده يومئذ سعيد بن خالد

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Hud's challenge includes the addressees and everyone with them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق قوله : فكيدوني جميعا اي فكيدوني أنتم ومن معكم جميعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r1.claim: The relative phrase refers to the idols, as confirmed by the collective address to plot against Hud in the next clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r1.anchor: ضمير الجمع المؤكد في قوله : { فكيدوني جميعا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r2.claim: His disavowal implies that the idols cannot harm him, so he challenges his people to plot; he addresses people, while including their idols in the challenge to meet their belief and complete their humiliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r2.anchor: فرع على البراءة جملة { فكيدوني جميعا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r3.claim: The command to plot is permission used as a taunt that exposes both idols' and people's inability, as in 77:39; it refutes their claim in 11:54.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r3.anchor: كناية عن التعجيز بالنسبة للأصنام وبالنسبة لقومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r4.claim: ثم marks a rise in rhetorical rank: after challenging them to plot, Hud tells them not to delay, expressing utmost contempt and that they cannot harm him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r4.anchor: ثم ارتقى في رتبة التعجيز والاحتقار فنهاهم عن التأخير بكيدهم إياه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.claim: Hūd openly disowns their idols and challenges them and their idols to plot against him; his challenge is described as a miracle because the numerous, powerful people could not harm him though he stood alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.anchor: فحينئذ جاهرهم هود عليه السلام بالتبري من أوثانهم وحضهم على كيده هم وأصنامهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r7.claim: Tunẓirūn means delay me: they are to act at once with whatever harm they can manage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r7.anchor: وتنظرون معناه تؤخروني أي عاجلوني بما قدرتم عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r1.claim: Hūd challenges his people and their idols to plot together to harm him without giving him a delay.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ فكيدوني جميعا ﴾ أي احتالوا أنتم وأوثانكم في ضري ثم لاتمهلون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls this a great sign of prophethood: a lone messenger challenges a united people who cannot harm him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا من أعظم آيات الرسل أن يكون الرسول وحده وأمته متعاونه عليه فيقول لهم كيدوني فلا يستطيع أحد منهم ضره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj links Hūd's challenge with Noah's challenge to his people and Muḥammad's challenge to his opponents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا من أعظم آيات الرسل أن يكون الرسول وحده وأمته متعاونه عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r4.claim: Hud challenges the people and their gods, if real, to plot against him together without delaying even a moment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r4.anchor: أي: أنتم وآلهتكم إن كانت حقا

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r6.claim: Kayd and makida mean scheming to do harm; the root originally concerns handling or working on something, and kayada bi-nafsihi can mean yielding up life.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r6.anchor: والكيد والمكيدة: الاحتيال في الشر، كاده يكيده كيدا، وأصله: المعالجة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r12.claim: Hud dares the people and their gods to act immediately, since he does not fear their power, and idols are inert and cannot harm or avenge themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r12.anchor: فإني لا أبالي بكم وبكيدكم ، ولا أخاف معزتكم وإن تعاونتم علي

MUQATIL:11:53-55/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r6.claim: The phrase refers to the gods worshipped besides God.

MUQATIL:11:53-55/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r7.claim: Hud challenges them and their gods together to plot against him without giving him any respite.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r1.claim: The phrase means associating gods with God; Hūd calls on them to witness his innocence of that association too.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r1.anchor: أى من إشراككم ألهة من دونه والمعنى إنى أشهد الله أنى برئ مما تشركون واشهدوا أنتم أيضا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r3.claim: Hūd challenges all his opponents and their gods to plot without delay; he fears neither conspiracy nor hostility.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ فكيدوني جميعا ﴾ أنتم وآلهتكم ﴿ ثم لا تنظرون ﴾ لا تمهلون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r4.claim: Their idols cannot harm or benefit; it is absurd to think they could retaliate by making Hūd mad after he rejected their worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r4.anchor: وكيف تضرنى آلهتكم وما هى إلا جماد لا يضرو لا ينفع وكيف تنتقم منى إذا نلت منها وصددت عن عبادتها بأن تخبلنى وتذهب بعقلى

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r4.claim: Hūd challenges his people and their idols to scheme together against him and harm him.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r4.anchor: أي أنتم وأوثانكم في عداوتي وضري.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r5.claim: Lā tunẓirūn means do not delay or give me respite.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r6.claim: Hūd’s challenge despite many enemies shows complete confidence in God’s help and is a sign of prophethood; the Prophet challenged Quraysh similarly, and Noah said to assemble their affair and partners.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r6.anchor: وهذا القول مع كثرة الأعداء يدل على كمال الثقة بنصر الله تعالى. وهو من أعلام النبوة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r1.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim says messengers became firm by contemplating the forelock-light that guides creation toward deeds God already knew; this explains Hūd’s confidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r1.anchor: ولهذا قويت الرسل وصاروا من أولي العزم لأنهم لاحظوا نور النواصي، وأيقنوا أن جميع خلقه منقادون بتلك الأنوار

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r8.claim: Hūd's challenge parallels Noah's challenge to gather his people and partners and give him no respite.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r8.anchor: وهذا نظير ما قاله نوح عليه السلام لقومه

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r9.claim: This is a decisive miracle: one man would not dare a great people to maximize their hostility and strike immediately unless sure God would protect him from their malice.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r9.anchor: وذلك أن الرجل الواحد إذا أقبل على القوم العظيم
